hypotheses.justification: Avoid constructing coequalizers. For u,v : T ⟶ X with u ≫ f = v ≫ f, put a = coprod.desc u v and q = coprod.desc (𝟙 T) (𝟙 T). The split epimorphism q is normal by normalEpiOfEpi, so it is a cokernel of some w with w ≫ q = 0. Coproduct identities give a ≫ f = q ≫ u ≫ f, hence (w ≫ a) ≫ f = 0. KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' applied to l implies w ≫ a = 0, since its kernel arrow is zero. CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' then gives d with q ≫ d = a. Precomposing with the two coproduct inclusions yields u = d = v. This uses no general cokernel existence and works unchanged for zero morphisms and trivial categories.
